decoder, where N is set to be significantly larger than the typical number of
objects in an image. One of the main difficulties of training is to score predicted
objects (class, position, size) with respect to the ground truth. Our loss produces
an optimal bipartite matching between predicted and ground truth objects, and
then optimize object-specific (bounding box) losses.

T ransformer encoder. First, a 1x1 convolution reduces the channel dimension
of the high-level activation map f from C to a smaller dimension d. creating a
new feature mapz0∈ Rd×H×W . The encoder expects a sequence as input, hence
we collapse the spatial dimensions ofz0 into one dimension, resulting in ad×HW
feature map. Each encoder layer has a standard architecture and consists of a
multi-head self-attention module and a feed forward network (FFN). Since the
transformer architecture is permutation-invariant, we supplement it with fixed
positional encodings [31,3] that are added to the input of each attention layer. We
defer to the supplementary material the detailed definition of the architecture,
which follows the one described in [47].

decoder. The decoder follows the standard architecture of the

We show that DETR achieves competitive results compared to Faster R-CNN
in quantitative evaluation on COCO. Then, we provide a detailed ablation
study of the architecture and loss, with insights and qualitative results. Fi-
nally, to show that DETR is a versatile and extensible model, we present results
on panoptic segmentation, training only a small extension on a fixed DETR
model. We provide code and pretrained models to reproduce our experiments at
https://github.com/facebookresearch/detr.

evidence.excerpt:
We presented DETR, a new design for object detection systems based on trans-
formers and bipartite matching loss for direct set prediction. The approach
achieves comparable results to an optimized Faster R-CNN baseline on the chal-
lenging COCO dataset. DETR is straightforward to implement and has a flexible
architecture that is easily extensible to panoptic segmentation, with competitive
results. In addition, it achieves significantly better performance on large objects
than Faster R-CNN, likely thanks to the processing of global information per-
formed by the self-attention.
This new design for detectors also comes with new challenges, in particular
regarding training, optimization and performances on small objects. Current
detectors required several years of improvements to cope with similar issues,
and we expect future work to successfully address them for DETR.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline results are measured with standard COCO AP and PQ metrics on held-out validation images, independent of the training loss used to optimize the model.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: COCO validation-set Average Precision and Panoptic Quality metrics computed against ground-truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Hungarian bipartite matching loss combining class log-likelihood, L1 box regression, and generalized IoU on training ground truth.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of matching Faster R-CNN performance while excelling on large objects are clearly substantiated by COCO evaluation metrics (e.g., Table 1 showing 42.0 AP with DETR matching Faster R-CNN while gaining +7.8 AP on large objects).
primary.evaluation_assessment: The method is rigorously benchmarked on COCO object detection and panoptic segmentation against competitive, heavily optimized Faster R-CNN and Panoptic FPN baselines, accompanied by systematic ablation studies of architectural components and losses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is carried out using standard benchmark metrics (COCO AP and PQ) on unseen validation images compared across varied architectural configurations and baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO evaluation protocol measuring Average Precision (AP, AP50, AP75, APS, APM, APL) and Panoptic Quality (PQ) against ground-truth validation annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Bipartite matching Hungarian loss combining class cross-entropy, L1 box regression, and generalized IoU (GIoU) loss on training ground truth labels.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly document that DETR lags behind on small objects (-5.5 AP compared to Faster R-CNN baselines), requires long training schedules (300-500 epochs), and saturates when the number of target instances approaches the fixed query limit.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the CNN backbone, transformer encoder-decoder with learned object queries, bipartite matching formulation via the Hungarian algorithm, and combined L1 and GIoU bounding box loss.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a foundational architectural paradigm shift for object detection with fully reproducible designs, transparent reporting of trade-offs, extensive ablation experiments, and rigorous benchmark evaluations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces DETR (DEtection TRansformer), a direct set prediction paradigm for object detection that eliminates anchor generation and non-maximum suppression (NMS) by using a transformer encoder-decoder and bipartite matching Hungarian loss.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a foundational architectural paradigm shift for object detection with fully reproducible designs, transparent reporting of trade-offs, extensive ablation experiments, and rigorous benchmark evaluations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly document that DETR lags behind on small objects (-5.5 AP compared to Faster R-CNN baselines), requires long training schedules (300-500 epochs), and saturates when the number of target instances approaches the fixed query limit.
